paragraphs.source_en: “If his tooth broke just from eating a shiitake mushroom, his teeth must be in a dreadful state. What do you think?” The master said to Meitei, “One could hardly call his teeth good. Wouldn’t you agree, Meitei?” Meitei said, “No, they are not good. Still, there is something rather charming about them. The fact that he still has not had the tooth put in makes it all the more amusing. Even now it serves as a place for Kuya mochi to catch; it is quite a spectacle.” Nose said, “Does he leave it broken that way because he has no spending money for a false tooth, or does he keep it broken out of eccentricity?” “Do not worry. He has not declared that he intends to style himself forever as a man with a missing front tooth.” So Meitei answered, gradually regaining his fondness for joking. Nose raised a new question: “If there is any letter or suchlike from the gentleman himself that has come to your house, I should like to see it.” “Postcards? We have plenty of those.” The master went to the study, brought back thirty or forty of them, and said, “Please have a look.” Nose said, “I need not look at so many; just two or three of them would...” Mr. Meitei said, “Here, let me choose some good ones for you.” With that, he picked out one of them and said, “This one should be amusing.” Nose said, “Oh, he draws pictures too? He is really quite deft! Let me see.” So saying, she examined it closely. “Oh my, how perfectly horrid! Isn’t this a badger spirit? Of all things, why did he have to draw a badger spirit? Still, it is not badly drawn; how strange, one can tell at once that it is a badger spirit.” Nose seemed somewhat impressed. The master said with a laugh, “Read what is written on it!” Nose began reading in the tone of a maidservant reading the newspaper: “On the night of New Year’s Eve by the old calendar, the badgers in the mountains held a garden party and danced without ceasing. Their song went: ‘Come along, come along / on New Year’s Eve / the mountain sightseers will not come / suppoko pon no pon! Pon, pon!” When Nose had finished reading, she said in great dissatisfaction, “What is this supposed to be? Isn’t he making a fool of people on purpose?” Meitei drew out another card and said, “Perhaps this heavenly maiden will please you?” When I looked, it showed a heavenly maiden wearing a robe of feathers and playing the biwa. Nose said, “This heavenly maiden’s nose is a little too small.” Meitei said, “No, that is just like ordinary people. Never mind the nose; read the words written there.” The words ran as follows: “Long ago there was an astronomer. One night, as usual, he climbed up onto a high platform and was gazing intently at the stars, when a beautiful heavenly maiden appeared in the sky and began to play music so exquisite that it could never be heard in this world. The astronomer forgot the cold that pierced him to the bone and listened in rapture. When morning came, the astronomer’s corpse was covered with pure white frost. That lying old man says this is a true story.” After reading it, Nose said, “What on earth is this? What meaning does it have? And this passes for a Bachelor of Science? He would be better off reading something like The Literary Club.” Kangetsu was thoroughly run down by her.

paragraphs.source_zh: “吃香菇就崩掉了牙，他的牙齿恐怕很糟吧。你们看呢？”主人对着迷亭说：“他的牙齿说不上好。迷亭君，对不对？”迷亭说：“是不好。不过，看上去也怪招人爱的哪。他的牙到今天也没有镶，这就更有意思啦，现在还粘着空也糕呢，真是奇观哩。”鼻子说：“是因为缺镶牙的零用钱，才就那样让牙齿缺下去的呢，还是故意与众不同才缺着的呢？”“请放心吧，他并没有宣称让牙永远缺下去。”迷亭回答着，逐渐恢复了他那爱开玩笑的兴头。鼻子又提出一个新问题：“要是他本人给府上来过什么书信之类的东西，我希望能看看。”“明信片嘛，那倒多得很。”主人去书斋里拿来了三四十张，说道：“请看吧。”鼻子说道：“倒也不用看那么多，看看其中的两三张，就……”迷亭先生说：“让我来给你挑几张好的吧。”说着他拣出其中的一张，说道：“这个，肯定有趣。”鼻子说：“哟，还画着画哪，手倒是真巧！让我看看。”说着她仔细端详起来。“哎哟，真恶心死啦！这不是‘狸精’吗？为什么别的不画，偏偏要画‘狸精’呢？可是，画得倒是不错，真怪，一看就知道是‘狸精’呢。”鼻子多少有些钦佩的样子。主人笑着说：“你念念上面写的字！”鼻子用女仆读报的腔调读起来：“旧历除夕之夜，山中狸精举行游园会，不断跳舞，其歌曰：‘来呀来／年三十的晚上／游山的人儿不会来的哟／嘶砰，𠳭砰！砰，砰！”鼻子念完，大为不满地说：“这算什么，这不故意涮人嘛？”迷亭又抽出一张来，说道：“你会喜欢这张仙女吧？”我一看，原来是画着一个仙女穿着羽衣在弹琵琶。鼻子说：“这个仙女的鼻子太小了点。”迷亭说：“不，和平常人一样嘛。且甭管鼻子，你还是念念写的词句吧。”它的词句是这样的：“古时候有一个天文学者，一天夜里，他照例又登上了高台，一心看着星星，这时空中出现了一位美丽的仙女，演奏世上绝对听不到的美妙音乐，天文学者忘了彻骨的寒冷，听得入了神。第二天清晨一看，那个天文学者的尸体上落满了白刷刷的霜花。那个喜爱扯谎的老头儿说这是个真实的故事哩。”鼻子念完后，说：“写的都是些什么，这有啥意思？这也算得上是个理学士呀。他最好还是读点什么《文章俱乐部》一类的东西才好呢。”寒月被她贬得一钱不值。
